propositions.text: Dismiss the Minister's appeal and confirm the RPD's determination that the Respondent is not excluded and is a Convention refugee
propositions.quote: These are my reasons for dismissing the Minister's appeal. I confirm the Refugee Protection Division's (RPD) determination that the Respondent is not excluded from refugee protection and that he is a Convention refugee.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the Minister's appeal and confirms the RPD's decision that the Respondent is not excluded and is a Convention refugee.

propositions.text: The Respondent is a Haitian citizen fearing persecution due to his sexual orientation and was deported from the US due to a criminal record
propositions.quote: The Respondent, XXXX XXXX, is a citizen of Haiti. He fears being persecuted due to his sexual orientation because he is gay. Prior to seeking protection in Canada, he lived for several years in the United States (US) before he was deported to Haiti because of his criminal record.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Respondent is Haitian, fears persecution for being gay, and was deported from the US due to a criminal record.

propositions.text: The Minister argues the Respondent is excluded from refugee protection for committing a serious non-political crime in the US
propositions.quote: The Minister intervened in the RPD hearing. The Minister argues that the Respondent is excluded from refugee protection because there are serious reasons for considering he committed a serious non-political crime in the US.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister argues the Respondent should be excluded from refugee protection for serious non-political crimes in the US.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Respondent is not excluded and faces a serious possibility of persecution in Haiti due to sexual orientation
propositions.quote: The RPD found the Respondent is not excluded. The RPD went on to determine that the Respondent faces a serious possibility of persecution in Haiti due to his sexual orientation.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Respondent not excluded and at risk of persecution in Haiti due to sexual orientation.

propositions.text: The Minister appealed the RPD decision, RAD rejected the appeal, Federal Court found procedural fairness denied and returned the appeal to RAD for redetermination
propositions.quote: The Minister appealed the RPD's decision. The Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) rejected the Minister's appeal. The Minister asked the Federal Court to review the RAD's decision. The Court found the Minister had been denied procedural fairness and returned the appeal to the RAD for redetermination.

propositions.text: This is the rehearing of the appeal of the RPD's original decision
propositions.quote: This is therefore the rehearing of the appeal of the RPD's original decision.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister appealed, RAD rejected appeal, Federal Court found procedural unfairness and returned the matter to RAD for rehearing.

propositions.text: No new evidence or oral hearing requested, so no jurisdiction to hold oral hearing
propositions.quote: Neither the Minister nor the Respondent have asked to admit any new evidence. I therefore have no jurisdiction to hold an oral hearing.

paragraphs.summary: No new evidence or oral hearing requested, so no jurisdiction to hold oral hearing.

propositions.text: The role is to review all evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision
propositions.quote: My role is to look at all the evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court's role is to review all evidence and decide if the RPD decision was correct.

propositions.text: A person may be excluded if there are serious reasons to consider they committed a serious non-political crime before coming to Canada
propositions.quote: A person may be excluded from refugee protection where there are serious reasons for considering they have committed a serious non-political crime prior to coming to Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The law states a person may be excluded if serious reasons exist to consider they committed a serious non-political crime before coming to Canada.

propositions.text: The Minister argues the RPD erred in finding the Respondent is not excluded but does not contest inclusion analysis
propositions.quote: The Minister's position is that the RPD erred in determining that the Respondent is not excluded. It has not contested the RPD's inclusion analysis.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister argues the RPD erred on exclusion but does not contest inclusion analysis.

propositions.text: Parties given opportunity to make submissions after Court returned matter to RAD; Respondent requested extension but denied as unnecessary
propositions.quote: The Respondent and the Minister were given the opportunity to make submissions after the Court returned this matter to the RAD. I also provided the parties with jurisprudence which I proposed to consider in my exclusion assessment. I put the parties on notice that if I determine the Respondent is not excluded, I may consider inclusion. Submissions were due on 18 February 2025. On 24 February 2025, the Respondent requested an extension of time to respond to the Notice. The Minister has not responded. I find it unnecessary to delay proceedings for further submissions from the Respondent as I have been able to reach a determination based on the material already on record. The application for an extension of time is therefore denied.

paragraphs.summary: The court gave parties chance to submit; Respondent's extension request denied as unnecessary; Minister did not respond.

propositions.text: Respondent is not excluded because crimes committed in US are not 'serious'
propositions.quote: I find the Respondent is not excluded because, in my assessment, the crimes he committed in the United States are not "serious".

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Respondent is not excluded because his US crimes are not serious.

propositions.text: Respondent was convicted of offences in US with no political connection
propositions.quote: The Minister provided evidence to show that the Respondent was convicted of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX offences in the US. There is no evidence that these crimes were connected in any way to a political objective. I find they are not political in nature.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister provided evidence of Respondent's convictions in US; crimes are not political in nature.

propositions.text: Details of first incident charges and sentencing are described but redacted
propositions.quote: Briefly, the circumstances of the offences are as follows: 1. On XXXX XXXX 2005, the Respondent was charged XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. The Respondent was accused of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX The Respondent XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and was sentenced to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX3

paragraphs.summary: The first incident's charges and sentencing details are described but redacted.

propositions.text: Details of second incident charges, accusations, sentencing, and Canadian robbery law are described but redacted
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX 2006, the Respondent was charged XXXX XXXX It is alleged XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX The Respondent was accused of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX The Respondent was charged XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and the Respondent XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX He was sentenced toXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX imprisonment XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.XXXXThe convictions themselves are not contested. The Minister asserts that the evidence is sufficient to establish serious reasons for considering that the Respondent committed robbery in both these incidents. In Canada, the crime of robbery is set out as follows: 343. Every one commits robbery who (a) steals, and for the purpose of extorting whatever is stolen or to prevent or overcome resistance to the stealing, uses violence or threats of violence to a person or property; (b) steals from any person and, at the time he steals or immediately before or immediately thereafter, wounds, beats, strikes or uses any personal violence to that person; 344. (1) Every person who commits robbery is guilty of an indictable offence and liable ... (b) ..., to imprisonment for life.4

paragraphs.summary: Second incident details and Canadian robbery law are described but redacted; Minister asserts evidence supports serious reasons for robbery.

propositions.text: Minister submits the crime is serious non-political crime and Respondent should be excluded
propositions.quote: The Minister submits that this is a serious non-political crime, and the Respondent should therefore be excluded.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister submits the crime is serious non-political and Respondent should be excluded.

propositions.text: Respondent testified denying involvement in first incident
propositions.quote: With respect to the first incident, the Respondent testified that he did not XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

paragraphs.summary: Respondent testified denying involvement in first incident.

propositions.text: Respondent admits involvement in second incident
propositions.quote: With regard to the second incident, the Respondent admits XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent admits involvement in second incident.

propositions.text: RPD found Respondent's testimony credible and preferred it over Minister's documentary evidence
propositions.quote: The RPD found the Respondent's testimony credible and preferred it over the documentary evidence submitted by the Minister. It found that, "... the Minister has not credibly established the facts supporting his application for exclusion ...", with regard to either incident.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found Respondent credible and Minister's evidence not credible for exclusion.

propositions.text: Conviction evidence meets threshold for serious reasons to consider offences committed, but issue is whether offences are 'serious' in Canada
propositions.quote: I agree with the Minister that the evidence of convictions meets the threshold of "serious reasons for considering" the Respondent committed offences in the US prior to coming to Canada. What is at issue is whether these offences would be considered "serious" if they were committed in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees convictions meet threshold for serious reasons but must decide if offences are 'serious' in Canada.

propositions.text: Respondent was not convicted of robbery; difference between robbery and theft explained; complainants' evidence not tested in court
propositions.quote: I note that the respondent was not convicted of robbery. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. In general, the difference between robbery and theft is that robbery involves the use or threat of some level of violence in the commission of the theft. The Minister relies on the evidence of the complainants as set out in the incident reports which indicate that the Respondent XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. I note the complainants' evidence was not tested in court in either incident. The first robbery charge was XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Respondent was not convicted of robbery; robbery differs from theft; complainants' evidence was untested in court.

propositions.text: Respondent pled guilty to first incident; court does not accept his minimization of responsibility
propositions.quote: With respect to the first incident, since the Respondent pled XXXX XXXX XXXX, I do not accept his contention that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: Respondent consistently minimized responsibility for offences in testimony before RPD
propositions.quote: I have listened to his testimony before the RPD. I find that he consistently minimized his responsibility for the offences.

propositions.text: Respondent's contention that he did not commit the offences is rejected
propositions.quote: I therefore also find the Respondent's contention that he did XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Respondent pled guilty, minimized responsibility, and rejects his denial of committing offences in first incident.

propositions.text: Minister need not prove conviction, only serious reasons to consider commission of robbery
propositions.quote: The Minister does not need to prove that the Respondent was convicted of robbery, merely that there are serious reasons for considering that he committed robbery.

propositions.text: Threshold for serious reasons is less than likelihood but more than suspicion
propositions.quote: This is a relatively low threshold: less than a likelihood but more than a mere suspicion.

propositions.text: Incident reports and original robbery charge meet threshold for serious reasons to consider commission of robbery
propositions.quote: I find the incident reports which include the statements of the security guards and the fact that the Respondent was originally charged with robbery, even though XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, is sufficient to meet this threshold.

propositions.text: There are serious reasons to consider Respondent committed offences considered robbery in Canada
propositions.quote: I find there are serious reasons for considering the Respondent committed offences which would be considered robbery if committed in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Court states Minister's low threshold met by incident reports and charges to consider Respondent committed robbery offences.

propositions.text: Issue is whether offences would be considered serious in Canada
propositions.quote: The issue is therefore whether these offences would be considered "serious" in Canada.

propositions.text: Offences committed by Respondent are not serious
propositions.quote: The offences committed by the Respondent are not serious

paragraphs.summary: Court identifies issue of seriousness in Canada and finds offences are not serious.

propositions.text: Offence punishable by 10+ years imprisonment indicates seriousness
propositions.quote: An offence punishable by a maximum term of imprisonment of at least 10 years is a strong indication that the crime is "serious".

propositions.text: Robbery punishable by life imprisonment generally considered serious
propositions.quote: Robbery, which is punishable by a maximum sentence of life imprisonment, is generally considered to be serious.

propositions.text: Ten-year rule must be applied contextually, not mechanistically
propositions.quote: However, this ten-year rule should be considered in context of the particular facts of the case and should not be applied in a mechanistic or unjust manner.

propositions.text: Presumption that robbery is serious can be rebutted
propositions.quote: It is possible to rebut the presumption that robbery is a serious crime.

paragraphs.summary: Court explains 10-year sentencing rule for seriousness, notes robbery usually serious but presumption can be rebutted.

propositions.text: Wide sentencing range means less serious crimes at low end should not be presumptively excluded
propositions.quote: Where the criminal provision in Canada has a large sentencing range, the upper end being ten years or more and the lower end being quite low, a person whose crime would fall at the less serious end of the range in Canada should not be presumptively excluded.

propositions.text: Assessing seriousness requires evaluating crime elements, prosecution mode, penalty, facts, mitigating/aggravating circumstances
propositions.quote: Assessing the seriousness of a crime requires an evaluation of the elements of the crime, the mode of prosecution, the penalty prescribed, the facts and the mitigating and aggravating circumstances underlying the conviction.

paragraphs.summary: Court states wide sentencing range requires contextual assessment of seriousness including crime elements and circumstances.

propositions.text: Robbery elements in Canada: stealing plus use/threat of violence
propositions.quote: The elements of robbery in Canada consist of stealing, and for the purpose of preventing or overcoming resistance to the stealing, the use of violence or threats of violence to a person.

propositions.text: Use or threat of violence as element militates toward seriousness
propositions.quote: The use or threat of violence as an element of robbery militates toward its being considered serious.

paragraphs.summary: Court outlines robbery elements and notes violence element supports seriousness.

propositions.text: Facts of offence show Respondent's actions would be minor theft but for certain factors
propositions.quote: In my assessment, but for the fact that the Respondent XXXX XXXX XXXX, the offence would have been considered a relatively minor theft.

propositions.text: Incident report describes offence as shoplifting
propositions.quote: In fact, the incident report itself describes it as "shoplifting."

propositions.text: Facts are neutral regarding seriousness of crime
propositions.quote: I find the facts are therefore neutral with respect to the seriousness of the crime.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds facts show offence akin to minor theft or shoplifting, neutral on seriousness.

propositions.text: Respondent convicted of felony though charges reduced
propositions.quote: Although the charges in the US were reduced, the Respondent was nonetheless convicted of a felony.

propositions.text: Robbery is indictable offence in Canada, generally more serious than summary offences
propositions.quote: In Canada, robbery is an indictable offence. Indictable offences are generally more serious than offences which may proceed summarily.

propositions.text: Mode of prosecution militates toward seriousness
propositions.quote: I find this a factor which militates towards being considered serious.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes felony conviction and indictable offence status militates toward seriousness.

propositions.text: Respondent convicted of lesser offence theft against person and sentenced to 7 months
propositions.quote: The Respondent was convicted of the lesser offence of theft against person and sentenced to 7 months.

propositions.text: Minister asserts robbery charge reduced due to plea bargain
propositions.quote: The Minister asserts this robbery charge was reduced to theft as a result of a plea bargain.

propositions.text: No evidence of plea bargain; prosecutor moved to reduce charges in interests of justice
propositions.quote: I see no evidence of any "bargain". The court documents referred to by the Minister show that the prosecutor moved to reduce the charges from a class 2 felony.

propositions.text: Respondent pled guilty on lawyer's advice to avoid robbery conviction and due to custody time
propositions.quote: The Respondent testified that he agreed to plead guilty on his lawyer's advice because it would avoid a robbery conviction and because he had already been in custody for several months.

propositions.text: Prosecutor likely reduced charges for interests of justice; sentence not inordinately lenient
propositions.quote: I find on the face of the record that the prosecutor most likely moved for the charges to be reduced because he was of the opinion it was in the interests of justice to do so. There is no evidence that the sentence passed was inordinately lenient or otherwise unjustified as the Minister suggests.

propositions.text: Low sentence militates against finding offence serious
propositions.quote: I find this is a relatively low sentence which militates toward a finding that the offence is not serious.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no plea bargain evidence; low sentence and charge reduction reflect justice interests, militating against seriousness.

propositions.text: No mitigating or aggravating circumstances raised by parties
propositions.quote: Neither party has raised any mitigating or aggravating circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes no mitigating or aggravating circumstances raised.

propositions.text: Robbery sentencing range in Canada is wide, max life imprisonment, no minimum except with weapon
propositions.quote: There is a very wide sentencing range for the offence of robbery in Canada. Although there is a maximum penalty of life imprisonment, there is no minimum sentence, except where a weapon is used in the commission of the robbery.

propositions.text: Use of weapon not an issue in this case
propositions.quote: Use of a weapon is not an issue in this case.

paragraphs.summary: Court states robbery sentencing range is wide with no minimum except for weapon use, which is not relevant here.

propositions.text: Where sentencing range is wide, must consider where crime falls in range
propositions.quote: Where there is a wide sentencing range, I need to consider where in that range the crime would fall.

propositions.text: Less serious crimes at low end should not be presumptively excluded; Article 1F(b) excludes only serious crimes
propositions.quote: A person, "... whose crime would fall at the less serious end of the range in Canada should not be presumptively excluded. Article 1F(b) is designed to exclude only those whose crimes are serious."

paragraphs.summary: Court states sentencing range requires assessing crime's position; less serious crimes should not be excluded under Article 1F(b).

propositions.text: Sentencing range not determinative; must look at similar cases to guide sentencing perspective in Canada
propositions.quote: The sentencing range is not determinative and is one of many factors. However, I must "look at similar cases as a guide to how the Applicant would be treated in Canada from the sentencing perspective" in order to avoid relying on a subjective notion of what is a serious crime in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Court explains sentencing range is one factor; similar cases guide Canadian sentencing perspective.

propositions.text: Maximum or significant custodial sentences reserved for use of weapon, serious injury, or larger criminal scheme
propositions.quote: The maximum sentence, or any significant custodial sentence, is generally reserved for those who, for example, use a weapon to commit the offence, seriously injure another, or participate in a larger criminal scheme.

propositions.text: None of these aggravating circumstances apply to Respondent
propositions.quote: None of these circumstances apply in the Respondent's case.

propositions.text: Likely sentence in Canada would be far lower than maximum life imprisonment
propositions.quote: I find that had this offence been committed in Canada, the actual sentence that would be imposed is likely to be far lower than the maximum of imprisonment for life.

propositions.text: Unlikely Respondent would face lengthy custody in Canada
propositions.quote: I find it unlikely that he would face a lengthy period of custody.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds aggravating factors absent; likely Canadian sentence much lower than life imprisonment, unlikely lengthy custody.

propositions.text: Canadian sentencing range for similar cases spans non-custodial to several months custody
propositions.quote: The sentencing range imposed in Canada for cases similar to the Respondent's span from receiving a non-custodial sentence up to perhaps several months in custody with lengthier sentences generally in cases where more serious violence or threat of violence is involved.

propositions.text: Respondent's actions would receive sentence well below maximum if committed in Canada
propositions.quote: In my view, accepting that the Respondent XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, his actions would receive a sentence well below the maximum prescribed if committed in Canada.

propositions.text: Likely sentence similar to actual US sentence of several months imprisonment
propositions.quote: I find it likely he would have received a sentence similar to that actually imposed in the US, in the range of several months' imprisonment.

propositions.text: This weighs heavily against finding crimes serious
propositions.quote: This weighs heavily against a finding that the Respondent's crimes are serious.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds likely Canadian sentence similar to US sentence, weighing against seriousness finding.

propositions.text: Presumption of seriousness rebutted for first offence in Houston, Texas
propositions.quote: When I weigh all of the relevant factors, I find the presumption of seriousness has been rebutted with respect to the first offence in Houston, Texas.

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes presumption of seriousness rebutted for first offence.

propositions.text: Use or threat of violence as element militates toward seriousness for second incident as well
propositions.quote: Here, as in the previous incident, the use or threat of violence as an element of robbery militates toward its being considered serious.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes violence element militates toward seriousness for second incident.

propositions.text: Facts of second offence show Respondent's actions would be minor theft but for certain factors
propositions.quote: Again, in my assessment, but for the fact that the Respondent XXXX XXXX XXXX, the offence would have been considered a relatively minor theft.

propositions.text: Facts neutral with respect to seriousness of crime for second incident
propositions.quote: I find the facts are therefore neutral with respect to the seriousness of the crime.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds facts of second offence neutral on seriousness, akin to minor theft.

propositions.text: Respondent originally charged with robbery, charge reduced
propositions.quote: The Respondent was originally charged with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX The charge was reduced to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

propositions.text: Robbery is indictable offence in Canada, militates toward seriousness
propositions.quote: In Canada, robbery is an indictable offence. I find this a factor which militates towards being considered serious.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes charge reduction and indictable offence status militates toward seriousness for second incident.

propositions.text: Prosecutor likely dismissed robbery charge in interests of justice
propositions.quote: Again, I find on the face of the record that the prosecutor most likely agreed for the robbery charge to be dismissed because he was of the opinion it was in the interests of justice to do so.

propositions.text: Not prepared to find sentence inordinately lenient or unjustified without more information
propositions.quote: Without more information I am not prepared to find that the sentence passed was inordinately lenient or otherwise unjustified

paragraphs.summary: Court finds prosecutor dismissed robbery charge for justice interests; no evidence sentence was unjustified.

propositions.text: The sentence is relatively low, suggesting the offence is not serious.
propositions.quote: I find this is a relatively low sentence which militates toward a finding that the offence is not serious.

propositions.text: No mitigating or aggravating circumstances were raised by either party.
propositions.quote: Neither party has raised any mitigating or aggravating circumstances.

propositions.text: The Respondent's XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is an aggravating factor.
propositions.quote: I find the fact that the Respondent's XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is an aggravating factor.

propositions.text: The Respondent's XXXX XXXX is a mitigating factor.
propositions.quote: I find his XXXX XXXX to be a mitigating factor.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the sentence low, no mitigating or aggravating circumstances raised by parties, but notes aggravating and mitigating factors in Respondent's conduct.

propositions.text: There is a very wide sentencing range for robbery offences in Canada.
propositions.quote: As discussed previously, there is a very wide sentencing range for the offence of robbery in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The court states that robbery offences in Canada have a very wide sentencing range.

propositions.text: The incident does not indicate a lengthy custodial sentence or life imprisonment is warranted.
propositions.quote: The XXXX XXXX incident does not XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX which would indicate a lengthy custodial sentence or imprisonment for life is warranted.

propositions.text: If committed in Canada, the sentence would likely be far lower than life imprisonment maximum.
propositions.quote: I find that had this offence been committed in Canada, the actual sentence that would be imposed is likely to be far lower than the maximum of imprisonment for life.

propositions.text: It is unlikely the Respondent would face a prolonged period of custody.
propositions.quote: I find it unlikely that he would face a prolonged period of custody.

propositions.text: Canadian sentencing range for similar cases spans from non-custodial to several months custody, longer for serious violence.
propositions.quote: As noted previously, the Canadian sentencing range for cases similar to the Respondent's span from receiving a non-custodial sentence up to perhaps several months in custody with lengthier sentences generally in cases where more serious violence or threat of violence is involved.

propositions.text: Accepting the Respondent struck the security guard, sentence would be well below maximum even as repeat offender.
propositions.quote: Again, accepting that the Respondent struck the security guard, his actions would receive a sentence well below the maximum prescribed if committed in Canada, even as a repeat offender.

propositions.text: Likely sentence similar to US sentence of several months imprisonment.
propositions.quote: I find it likely he would have received a sentence similar to that actually imposed in the US, in the range of several months' imprisonment.

propositions.text: This weighs heavily against finding the Respondent's crimes are serious.
propositions.quote: This weighs heavily against a finding that the Respondent's crimes are serious.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the offence would not warrant lengthy custody in Canada, likely a short sentence similar to US, weighing against seriousness.

propositions.text: The presumption of seriousness is rebutted regarding the Respondent's offence.
propositions.quote: When I consider all of the relevant factors, I find the presumption of seriousness has been rebutted with respect to the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the presumption of seriousness is rebutted for the Respondent's offence.

propositions.text: The Respondent is not excluded under Article 1F(b) of the Convention and section 98 of IRPA.
propositions.quote: For these reasons, the Respondent is not excluded under Article 1F(b) of the Convention and section 98 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Respondent is not excluded from protection under Article 1F(b) and section 98 IRPA.

propositions.text: The Minister makes no submissions on inclusion or Convention refugee status based on sexual orientation.
propositions.quote: The Minister makes no submissions on the RPD's findings with respect to inclusion and that the Respondent is a Convention refugee based on his sexual orientation.

propositions.text: The court agrees with the RPD's assessment that the Respondent is a Convention refugee based on sexual orientation.
propositions.quote: I have conducted my own assessment, and I agree with the RPD's assessment.

propositions.text: Significant time has passed since the RPD decision, so the court considered updated objective documentation on Haiti.
propositions.quote: I note that a significant amount of time has passed since the RPD rendered its decision. I have therefore considered the objective documentation with respect to Haiti to determine whether there has been a significant change in circumstances that would warrant coming to a different conclusion.

propositions.text: The situation for sexual minorities in Haiti has not changed significantly since the RPD's determination.
propositions.quote: I find the situation for sexual minorities in Haiti has not changed significantly since the RPD's determination.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister made no submissions on inclusion; the court agrees with RPD that Respondent is a Convention refugee and finds no significant change in Haiti's situation.

propositions.text: The Minister's appeal is dismissed.
propositions.quote: I dismiss the Minister's appeal.

propositions.text: The RPD was correct that the Respondent is not excluded and is a Convention refugee.
propositions.quote: The RPD was correct in determining that the Respondent is not excluded from protection and that he is a Convention refugee.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the Minister's appeal and upholds the RPD's decision that the Respondent is not excluded and is a Convention refugee.
